finding: An arrow function as the value of a class field, such as `f = (a) => (a > 0 ? 1 : 2);`, still stops the TypeScript measure with exit 1: "the complexity at line 2 pairs with no single function". This is the case of IMPL-0106 for a PropertyDefinition. The ESLint rule complexity reports the function at the field key, before the range of the arrow. The fix of IMPL-0106 takes the parent as the outer node only for a Property, so the arrow of a class field still pairs with no range. The code at 8c4bc215 failed the same way, so the fix did not cause it. Reproduction: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-matthiasdaues-Documents-datenschoenheit-agent-factory/89fd1670-49e4-4a59-97db-e1035150aa04/scratchpad/st0449-review/repro_typescript.sh <command> class-field. Fix: in the rule crap/range, also take a parent PropertyDefinition as the outer node when its value is the function. Add the case to test_cg_13_a_function_expression_as_an_object_value_gets_a_row.
why_this_severity: The command exists only on the story branch. The current TypeScript code of this repository has no class field with a function, and the measure stops loudly instead of reporting a wrong row (no to fails_purpose). The first story that adds such a field gets a blocked run whose message does not name the cause.
